title: The SpaceSquat Wiki
subtitle: Bureau-approved. Inaccuracies are your fault.
note: Draft lore. Names and details are placeholders until the gameplay loop for each organization is built. Edit this file; the in-game wiki (L), docs/WIKI.md and the project wiki all come from it.

organizations.name: Vantablack Holdings
organizations.does: Landlord-finance conglomerate. Holds the Spine's founding charter and most of the debt in orbit. Runs the Science Centre.
organizations.lore: Vantablack never builds anything. It owns the paper that says who may. When the Spine was poured, Vantablack held the charter, and it has been charging rent on the void ever since. Its Science Centre has been 'testing' whether EVA is survivable for eleven years; the results are always 'promising'.
organizations.rumour: Nobody has ever seen a Vantablack executive. Nobody has ever seen the eleven years of test results either.
organizations.renameNote: Placeholder name: 'Vantablack' is a real trademark. Rename before launch.

organizations.name: Kessler Mining Co.
organizations.does: Asteroid mining and salvage. Strips derelicts, buys and sells scrap, runs the Refit Bays where skiffs are fitted out.
organizations.lore: Kessler started by mining asteroids and finished by mining everything else. Every wreck, every abandoned skiff, every ship that wasn't nailed down eventually passes through a Kessler furnace. Its Refit Bays will bolt anything to anything, as long as you pay in scrap.
organizations.stamp: Fit any upgrade to your skiff.
organizations.rumour: The debris field around the Spine is Kessler's. They seeded it. Business was slow.

organizations.name: Ash & Iron
organizations.does: Heavy industry: foundries, refineries, smelters. The smog, the slag vents and most of the jobs nobody wants.
organizations.lore: Ash & Iron is half factory, half church. Shifts begin with a hymn and end when the quota is met, which is never. Its foundries smelt Kessler's scrap into the girders the Spine keeps growing. The smog over the city is technically an Ash & Iron product, and it is trademarked.
organizations.rumour: The hymn has a verse for every worker who died on shift. It is very long.

organizations.name: Null Sector Trust
organizations.does: Security and insurance. Owns the patrol drones, the impound yards and, soon, detention. Insures the corps against the people.
organizations.lore: Null Sector sells two products: protection, and protection from Null Sector. Its drones are the only police on the Spine, and they are paid per capture. Stolen ships go to Null Sector impound; so, eventually, does everything else.
organizations.stamp: Get processed: survive a 1-star pursuit or pay a token fine.
organizations.rumour: The drones are cheaper than the fines they collect. Null Sector has never once lost money.

organizations.name: Cinder Collective
organizations.does: Utilities cartel: air, water, oxygen, power. Everything you breathe is metered, and the Collective owns the meter.
organizations.lore: The Cinder Collective calls itself a co-operative, and technically every resident is a member, because every resident breathes. Membership dues are deducted per breath. The Meter Office registers new pilots for their ration of air and water, which is enough to work and not quite enough to argue.
organizations.stamp: Register for your air, water and oxygen ration.
organizations.rumour: The air in Tenure Heights isn't metered. The Collective calls this 'a pilot programme'.

organizations.name: Gullet Provisions
organizations.does: Food. Runs the Ration Depots, the protein vats and the only restaurant on the Spine (members only).
organizations.lore: Gullet feeds everyone, in the sense that everyone eats what Gullet makes. Ration bricks come in three flavours: Original, Original Plus, and Thursday. The Ration Depot hands out a pilot's first ration free, as a 'gesture'; the gesture is recorded as a debt.

organizations.name: Last Mile Freight
organizations.does: Freight and logistics. Posts the courier jobs, owns the Freight Depot, and subcontracts all risk to you.
organizations.lore: Last Mile owns no ships and employs no pilots. It owns the jobs. Every crate on the Spine moves through its board, and every pilot who hauls one is an independent contractor, which means the cargo is insured and the pilot is not.
organizations.rumour: The 'sealed casket' jobs pay double. Do not open the sealed casket.

organizations.name: Gavel & Rope
organizations.does: Auctioneers. Runs the Auction House where dormant skiff numbers and seized property are sold. Every auction lasts 69 hours.
organizations.lore: Gavel & Rope sells what other people lose. Dormant skiff numbers, evicted homes, impounded ships: if it has been taken from someone, it goes under the gavel. Every auction runs exactly 69 hours. Nobody at Gavel & Rope will say why.
organizations.stamp: Place a bid (any amount of in-game currency).

organizations.name: Mercy Unlimited
organizations.does: Medical, funerary and sponsorship. Sponsors the Spine Run, processes deaths and keeps the death count.
organizations.lore: Mercy Unlimited heals you, buries you, and sponsors the race that makes both more likely. Its name is on the Spine Run gate, every clinic and every death notice. When a pilot dies (deletes their account), Mercy files the paperwork and the Registry announces the number.
organizations.stamp: Finish one lap of the Spine Run.
organizations.rumour: Mercy pays a bonus to the Spine Run's sponsor-of-record for every crash. Mercy is the sponsor-of-record.

organizations.name: Ministry of the Gentry
organizations.does: Allocates Tenure Heights housing, registers the gentry, collects rent from scrappers living there, and runs affirmative action.
organizations.lore: The Ministry exists to guarantee equality: everyone has equal access to everything, and the gentry have it conveniently. Its only office is, for reasons of 'community engagement', deep inside the slum's heat zone. Gentry must drive in to register; scrappers who make it there during an unannounced allocation may be offered one of thirteen permanent homes.
organizations.stamp: Get your residency stamp. Mind the hazards.
organizations.rumour: Somebody once held a Sprawl hut and a Tenure unit at the same time. The Ministry calls it a clerical error.

organizations.name: The Assessor's Office
organizations.does: Keeps the Land Registry and the public ledger. Enforces the 1.13× rule: any lot, any time, owner can't refuse.
organizations.lore: The Assessor decides what everything is worth, and the answer is always 1.13 times what you paid. Its ledger is the only honest document on the Spine, because it is the only one nobody can afford to bribe. Anyone may read it. Almost nobody does.
organizations.stamp: Read the ledger. No purchase necessary.
organizations.rumour: The Assessor has never assessed itself.

organizations.name: Registry of Skiffs & Souls
organizations.does: Issues skiff numbers from #001, keeps the Sprawl Housing Registry, records deaths, and releases dormant numbers to auction after 13 days.
organizations.lore: The Registry gives every pilot a skiff and a number, and the number is the important part. It never sells numbers; it only releases them, after thirteen days of silence, to Gavel & Rope. It also runs the Sprawl Housing Registry, because a soul needs a hovel to be counted.
organizations.rumour: Skiff #000 exists. It is not on the Registry.

organizations.name: Bureau of Public Cheer
organizations.does: Morale, propaganda and the daily Corp Bulletin. Administers the Compliance Oath.
organizations.lore: The Bureau writes the Corp Bulletin, schedules the weather, and measures public cheer to two decimal places. New residents swear the Compliance Oath at the Bulletin Tower. The oath is thirteen lines long. Nobody remembers line nine, and the Bureau prefers it that way.
organizations.rumour: This wiki is published by the Bureau.

places.name: The Spine (Avenue Zero)
places.text: The main drag: 13 blocks of 13 lots (169), all on the north side, 42 km end to end. Any lot can be bought at 1.13× its value; towers start at 13 floors and grow every time one changes hands, to 100 (the one number that isn't 13). The 12 gaps between blocks are crossings you can fly through north-south; proper roads and intersections are coming.

places.name: The Atlas
places.text: Block 7, the centre of the Spine, named for the first vertebra, the one that holds up the head. Every distance in the city is measured from it.

places.name: The Nerves
places.text: On a real spine, nerves branch out between the vertebrae, never through them. The Prime Rogue Nerve runs north from the crossing between blocks 6 and 7 to Prime Rogue's campus; the Wilco Nerve runs south from the crossing between blocks 7 and 8 to Wilco's. The Spine itself is never cut.

places.name: The Architects' campuses
places.text: Prime Rogue's (north) and Wilco's (south), each at the end of its Nerve, each with a four-lot, 130-floor tower that can never be bought.

places.name: Lower Upper Squalor & Upper Lower Squalor
places.text: The two Sprawls, each about a minute's flight past a city limit: Lower Upper Squalor to the east, Upper Lower Squalor to the west. Near-identical: 39 sites each (13 × 3). Scrap-built huts in 13 tiers, from Lean-to to The Big Bunker, never branded. Each has a Housing Registry on its city-facing edge.

places.name: The Mercy Unlimited Raceway
places.text: Two circuits in the void south of the main drag, built to the shapes of tracks from a planet nobody here remembers: The Island Circuit (after Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve, Montréal) and The Temple Circuit (after Monza). 13 gates a lap. Mercy Unlimited sponsors both, and the crashes.

places.name: Tenure Heights
places.text: The gentry's gated, domed deck north of the Spine. Equal access to everything, conveniently. Scrappers may enter. Null Sector will notice. (Coming.)

places.name: The void
places.text: Everything between. Buoys mark the way to the Sprawls. Debris courtesy of Kessler.

glossary.text: Prime Rogue Inc. and Wilco Corporation, who built the universe. Their two 130-floor towers can never be bought.
Block 7, the centre of the Spine. All distances are measured from it.
A north-south road branching off the Spine at a crossing. The first two lead to the Architects' campuses.
In-game currency, earned only by playing. Pays for upgrades, huts, rent and bids. Never bought, never cashed out.
What you receive when someone buys your lot. Spend them on other lots. They never expire and never become cash.
Your ship, issued at signup with a number from #001. Handles like a shopping cart full of scrap until you fix it.
Anyone holding a lot or credits. Lose your lots and hold only credits for 13 days and you rejoin the people.
Deleting your account. Deaths are counted and announced by skiff number only.
Everything is 13, except the maximum building height. Nobody knows why.

Your level before Level 1. Each of the 13 organizations stamps your residency card once (C): 0.01 per stamp, 0.00 → 0.13. The 13th stamp makes you Level 1, “Fully Processed”. Ten stamps come from desks on the Spine (one per block); Kessler, Mercy and the Registry stamp you at the Refit Bay, the Spine Run gate and the Housing Registries.

recreation_note: 13 designated recreation zones. Zones 1–8 are Kevin's; 9–13 are suggestions until confirmed. Every zone gets a record board (local bests now, global leaderboards with the server).

recreation.name: The Redundant Terrestrial Gravitational Driving Range
recreation.activity: Drive actual cars, on wheels, under simulated planetary gravity. Lap times on a record board.
recreation.lore: Last Mile built it to test delivery vans for planets nobody delivers to anymore. The gravity is fake, the asphalt is fake, and the nostalgia is extremely real.

recreation.name: The Official Church of 13
recreation.lore: The state faith. Services last 13 minutes, there are 13 commandments, and the collection plate takes exactly 13 scrap. Nobody knows why it's 13. Doubting it is not recommended.

recreation.name: The Underground Church of the Dog
recreation.activity: Worship the dog. Literally, a dog.
recreation.lore: The minority religion, and the badass one. Meets in a hollowed-out Kessler ore hauler under the Spine. The dog is a good boy. The dog has always been a good boy. Null Sector pretends not to know where it is.

recreation.name: The Collective Fauna & Flora Regeneration Center
recreation.activity: Run the obstacle course for the record board. Eat some genuinely disgusting food.
recreation.lore: The last living things on the Spine, kept in a dome and used as an obstacle course. The café serves 'regenerated' cuisine. Do not ask what was regenerated.

recreation.name: Black Site Number 13
recreation.host: Null Sector Trust (officially does not exist)
recreation.activity: You can't go in. Fly close and you hear screams. Walk up to the fence and there's a machine: a scrap-themed game of Snake.
recreation.lore: There is no Black Site Number 13. The screaming is ambient audio. The Snake machine is a recreational amenity. Your high score has been noted.

recreation.name: The AstroTurf Center for Community Formation
recreation.activity: TBD. Suggestion: organise a 'spontaneous grassroots' rally in under 13 minutes (recruit NPCs, hand out pre-printed signs, hit the cheer quota).
recreation.lore: Where communities are formed, professionally. All spontaneity is scheduled in advance.

recreation.name: The Non-Volunteer Volunteer Militia
recreation.host: Chartered by the corps (you swear allegiance to one)
recreation.activity: Weekly shooting qualification. Skip it and you're fined scrap. Go as often as you like. Has its own rank progression (separate roadmap track).
recreation.lore: Membership is voluntary and mandatory. Every resident is a volunteer; every volunteer qualifies weekly; every absence is invoiced. The truly devoted rise through the ranks of their corporation's company.

recreation.name: The Innocuous Center for Imaging Research
recreation.host: Vantablack Holdings × Mercy Unlimited (medical) / Null Sector Trust (military)
recreation.activity: Hidden-object mini-game. Medical track: find it in a body (X-ray scans). Military track: find it on a map.
recreation.lore: Nothing about this building is suspicious. The scans are anonymised. The maps are of nowhere in particular. The objects are whatever you find.

recreation.name: Kessler Demolition Pit
recreation.activity: Bumper-skiff derby in a ring of wrecks. Last skiff still flying wins.
recreation.lore: Kessler calls it 'pre-salvage'. Everything that loses gets smelted by morning.

recreation.name: Ash & Iron Hall of Hymns
recreation.activity: Rhythm game to the factory hymn. Every verse is a worker who died on shift; the song gets longer.
recreation.lore: Shifts begin with the hymn. The hall is where you practise, because getting it wrong on the floor is a disciplinary matter.

recreation.name: Gullet's Thursday Eat-Off
recreation.activity: Competitive eating of Thursday-flavoured ration bricks. Timing and stamina mini-game.
recreation.lore: The prize is more Thursday. Nobody has ever found out what's in it, but the record holder has a theory.

recreation.name: Gavel & Rope Appraisal Parlour
recreation.activity: Guess what a piece of junk is worth; closest without going over beats the Assessor. Pure skill, no stakes.
recreation.lore: The Assessor is always right. Beating the Assessor is therefore impossible, and the record board is mostly people who did it anyway.

recreation.name: Cinder Breath-Hold Pool
recreation.activity: Hold your breath for as long as you can. Ties into the oxygen ration.
recreation.lore: The Collective's most popular attraction: the only place on the Spine where not breathing is free.

architects_note: Out of game: Prime Rogue Inc. is the real company that operates SpaceSquat. The two towers are the operator's own buildings and sit outside the market.
architects_intro: The two companies that built the universe. They sit above the 13 organizations, own the only two buildings that can never be bought, and behave more like NPCs than players. Each has a campus just off the Atlas, reached by its own Nerve: Prime Rogue to the north, Wilco to the south. Each tower covers four lots and stands 130 floors (13 × 10). No other building may be taller; everyone else stops at 100.

architects.name: Prime Rogue Inc.
architects.lore: Co-builder of the universe. Prime Rogue drew the plans for the Spine, the void and the rules, then published all of them, which nobody had ever done before. Its tower stands 130 floors so that there is always someone watching the watchers. The 13 organizations say other things about it, quietly. Prime Rogue is named for Rogue, the first dog. Rogue is not dead, only away.
rumours: Every transaction on the Spine is in Prime Rogue's ledger. The Assessor's ledger is a copy.
The lights on the top floor are left on for someone who is coming back.

architects.name: Wilco Corporation
architects.lore: Prime Rogue's partner. Nobody has ever seen a Wilco employee, and Wilco's only public statement is its motto. Its tower matches Prime Rogue's floor for floor. Wilco is named for Wilco, the living dog, who carries out frequent daily inspections of the Spine and the Sprawls, sniffs everything, and leaves goodies behind for whoever finds them first. Null Sector drones will not engage Wilco. Nobody has asked them why.
rumours: Pilots who learn the inspection route eat well. (Inspections: coming.)
